title: Build mime-tree and smime-tree workspace
description: Two standalone Rust crates need to be built from scratch: mime-tree (RFC 5322/MIME parser producing a byte-range-indexed part tree) and smime-tree (S/MIME sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt via key traits). Both must pass quality gates (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests) and satisfy all CLAUDE.md invariants: no JMAP, no async, no unsafe beyond transitive RustCrypto, owned lifetime-free public types, MSRV 1.75.
design:
No hand-spun parsers, no hand-spun crypto. Every parser and every cryptographic primitive must come from an existing crate.

Parsers: mail-parser (RFC 5322/MIME), cms (CMS/DER), x509-cert (certificates), der (DER encode/decode)
Transfer decoders: base64 crate, quoted_printable crate
Charset: encoding_rs
Crypto primitives: rsa, p256, p384, aes+cbc, aes-gcm, sha2, x963-kdf, aes-kw
Randomness: rand_core::OsRng — NOT the top-level rand crate. rand_core is the minimal CSPRNG interface used throughout RustCrypto; OsRng satisfies CryptoRngCore which all RustCrypto primitives accept.
Cert chain validation: x509-cert path building or webpki — research required, do not hand-roll

The one acceptable place for manual text formatting is MIME header/boundary generation in sign() and encrypt() output — that is not parsing or crypto.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test --workspace passes clean; cargo clippy --workspace -D warnings passes; both crates compile on MSRV 1.75; all public types are Serialize+Deserialize with no lifetime params
notes: Review converged after 3 round(s). Final review: MIME-596.
